mainTopic: The process of גירות (conversion) as taught in a ברייתא: the final words of warning, מילה, טבילה, the procedure for a woman, and how עבד משוחרר and נדה compare to a גר
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about how בית דין accepts a גר. The convert is warned about מצוות, then has מילה right away, and after healing he goes to טבילה in front of תלמידי חכמים; after that he is fully Jewish. A woman immerses modestly, and an עבד משוחרר and a נדה share the same מקוה and חציצה rules. The גמרא then goes back over the ברייתא line by line. It explains that the warnings let an unserious candidate drop out, and that the gifts to the poor are stressed because a non-Jew is so strict about property. It also explains that we stop warning once he is determined, learned from נעמי and רות. Then it explains why the מילה is not delayed, which shreds invalidate it, why we wait for healing, and that the ברייתא should read three scholars, not two. It teaches that a convert who goes back to his old ways is still Jewish, so his קידושין work. Finally, רב ששת settles whether a freed slave must accept the מצוות by tying the two ברייתות to the רבנן and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, in a ברייתא about the יפת תואר that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the warning: no huge reward or punishment in this world, and do not overwhelm him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes telling the convert that ישראל in the present time cannot receive a large share of good or of punishment in this world. It adds that בית דין should not pile too much on him or be too exacting.
steps.simpleTranslation: [ישראל at this time are not able to receive] either an abundance of good or an abundance of punishment. And they do not overwhelm him, and they are not exacting with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing what בית דין tells a convert about reward and punishment. It then sets a tone of gentleness: do not overwhelm him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main reward and punishment are saved for עולם הבא, so the convert should not expect great good, or great suffering, right now. Then comes a rule about how to talk to him: give him a fair picture without scaring him off with too much detail or too many threats.

keyTerms.meaning: An abundance of good (reward)
Punishment, calamity
They do not overwhelm him (with too much talk or too many warnings)
They are not exacting with him (about every fine detail)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new idea. The sentence picks up in the middle of the ברייתא's speech to the convert, which began before this section.

phrases.english: Not an abundance of good
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started earlier: ישראל at this time are not able to receive...

phrases.english: and not an abundance of punishment.
And they do not overwhelm him,
and they are not exacting with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא רוֹב טוֹבָה וְלֹא רוֹב פּוּרְעָנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's speech to the convert, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reward and punishment are mainly in עולם הבא, and בית דין should not overwhelm the convert or be overly exacting with him.

steps.title: If he accepts, he is circumcised right away, and again if pieces remain
steps.stepSummary: Once the convert accepts everything, they do מילה immediately. If leftover shreds of skin still make the מילה invalid, they cut again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he accepted, they circumcise him immediately. If shreds that invalidate the circumcision remained on him, they circumcise him again a second time.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from the talk to action. Once the convert agrees, the first physical step is מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no waiting period after he accepts: מילה happens right away. The ברייתא adds a practical case. If ציצין that block a valid מילה are left, the job is not finished and must be completed.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted (all that was told to him)
They circumcise
Shreds of foreskin left after circumcision
That hold back, meaning they make it invalid

phrases.english: If he accepted, they circumcise him immediately.
If shreds remained on him
that invalidate the circumcision,
they go back and circumcise him a second time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the warnings, the ברייתא moves to the first act of conversion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is done right after acceptance, and it is repeated if invalidating ציצין remain.

steps.title: After healing, he immerses with two scholars teaching him מצוות
steps.stepSummary: Once he heals from the מילה, they do טבילה right away. Two תלמידי חכמים stand by and teach him some light and some serious מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he healed, they immerse him immediately, and two Torah scholars stand over him and inform him of some light מצוות and some serious מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second physical step, טבילה, which comes after he heals from the מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is fixed: first מילה, then healing, then טבילה. While he is immersing, two תלמידי חכמים teach him a sample of light and serious מצוות again, so he enters Judaism with the commandments in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: He healed
They immerse (him in a מקוה)
Torah scholars
Light (lenient) and serious (stringent) מצוות

phrases.english: Once he healed, they immerse him immediately.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים עוֹמְדִים עַל גַּבָּיו
phrases.english: And two Torah scholars stand over him
and inform him of some light מצוות
and some serious מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the מילה with the next stage, טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טבילה happens right after the מילה heals, with two תלמידי חכמים present to teach him some מצוות.

steps.title: After immersing, he is fully Jewish
steps.stepSummary: Once he immerses and comes up, the convert counts as a full Jew in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He immersed and came up: he is like a Jew in all respects.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the result of the process for a man: after טבילה, the גירות is complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The moment of change is coming up out of the water. From then on, he is not a 'half Jew' or a Jew on probation. He is like any born Jew in every halachic matter.

keyTerms.meaning: He immersed and came up out of the water
Like a Jew in every respect

steps.whatToRemember: The order of גירות for a man: acceptance, then מילה (repeated if needed), healing, טבילה in front of two תלמידי חכמים. After that he is fully Jewish.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the exact moment a convert's status changes, which matters for every halacha that depends on being Jewish, such as marriage and testimony.

phrases.english: Once he immersed and came up,
he is like a Jew in all respects.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָבַל וְעָלָה — הֲרֵי הוּא כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְכׇל דְּבָרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the description of a man's conversion by stating his new status.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After טבילה, the convert is a full Jew in every respect.

steps.title: How a woman immerses, with modesty kept
steps.stepSummary: For a woman, other women seat her in the water up to her neck. The two תלמידי חכמים stand outside and teach her some light and some serious מצוות from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman: women seat her in water up to her neck, and two Torah scholars stand outside for her and inform her of some light מצוות and some serious מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains how the טבילה step works for a female convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two תלמידי חכמים are still needed, just as for a man. To protect her צניעות, women handle her in the water and the scholars stay outside. Everything else, including teaching her מצוות, stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the women) seat her
Up to her neck
Outside

steps.confusionAlert: The scholars standing outside is a change in how the step is carried out, not in what is required. Two scholars are still part of her טבילה, just as for a man.

phrases.english: A woman: women seat her
in water up to her neck,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים עוֹמְדִים לָהּ מִבַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: and two Torah scholars stand outside for her,
and they inform her of some light מצוות
and some serious מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה — נָשִׁים מוֹשִׁיבוֹת אוֹתָהּ בְּמַיִם עַד צַוָּארָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the טבילה step to a woman, changing how it is done so it stays modest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female convert is seated in the water by women, while two תלמידי חכמים teach her מצוות from outside.

steps.title: The same process applies to a freed slave
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says these rules apply both to a גר and to an עבד משוחרר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both a convert and a freed slave [follow this procedure].
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא widens the rule: everything said about the convert's טבילה applies to a freed slave too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד כנעני who is set free becomes a full Jew through טבילה at the time he is freed. So his טבילה follows the same procedure as a convert's.

keyTerms.meaning: A freed (emancipated) slave
Both this one and that one (the same rule for both)

phrases.english: Both a convert and a freed slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the convert's procedure to a freed slave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A freed slave's טבילה follows the same procedure as a convert's.

steps.title: Same מקוה and same חציצה rules for גר, freed slave and נדה
steps.stepSummary: A גר and an עבד משוחרר immerse in the same kind of מקוה as a נדה. Anything that counts as a barrier for regular טבילה also counts as one for all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the place where a menstruating woman immerses, there a convert and a freed slave immerse. And anything that interposes in immersion interposes for a convert, a freed slave, and a menstruating woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by tying conversion טבילה to regular טבילה, both in where it is done and in what can invalidate it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two comparisons are made. First, the place: a valid מקוה, the kind a נדה uses. Second, חציצה: anything between the body and the water that would invalidate a regular טבילה also invalidates the טבילה of a גר, a freed slave, or a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her menstrual state who must immerse
Immerses / they immerse
Interposes, forms a barrier between the body and the water
Ritual immersion

steps.whatToRemember: The טבילה of a גר or עבד משוחרר follows the same rules as a נדה's: a proper מקוה and no חציצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because these rules are shared, a flawed מקוה or a barrier on the body could invalidate a conversion, just as it would invalidate a נדה's טבילה.

phrases.english: And in the place where a menstruating woman immerses,
phrases.notes: He means a proper מקוה, kosher for a נדה.

phrases.english: there a convert and a freed slave immerse.
And anything that interposes in immersion,
interposes for a convert, a freed slave, and a menstruating woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִמְקוֹם שֶׁנִּדָּה טוֹבֶלֶת, שָׁם גֵּר וְעֶבֶד מְשׁוּחְרָר טוֹבְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the comparison of גר and freed slave by tying their טבילה to a נדה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר and an עבד משוחרר immerse in a נדה's kind of מקוה, and the same חציצה rules apply to all three.

steps.title: Back to the ברייתא: the first conversation with a would-be גר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening of the ברייתא: the בית דין asks the גר why he wants to convert and tells him some light and some serious מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: When a person comes to convert, they say to him: 'What made you decide to come and convert?' And they let him know some light מצוות and some serious מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא it quoted earlier and picks up its first line in order to explain it. This is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before any מילה or טבילה, the בית דין starts with a conversation. They check his reasons, and they give him a small, balanced taste of what Jewish life demands, both light and serious מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": the גמרא is quoting a source it already brought, so it can analyze it
To convert, to become a גר
"What did you see?": what made you decide this?
Light (easier) מצוות and serious (stricter) מצוות

phrases.english: The Master said: A convert who comes to convert,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: מָה רָאִיתָ שֶׁבָּאתָ לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר?
phrases.english: they say to him: What did you see that you came to convert?
And they inform him of some light מצוות
and some serious מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the start of the ברייתא (whose later parts were covered in steps 1-7) to explain its opening line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית דין asks the גר his motive and tells him some light and some serious מצוות.

steps.title: Why tell him the מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is for telling the גר about the מצוות at this early stage.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the בית דין bothers telling him the מצוות before he converts. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling him the hard parts might seem like it scares people away. The גמרא wants to know the purpose behind this.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is the reason?": the גמרא asks for the logic behind a rule

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the בית דין informs the would-be גר about מצוות before converting him.

steps.title: So that if he will drop out, he drops out now
steps.stepSummary: The answer: if he is going to back away, it is better that he backs away now, before he converts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if he is going to pull away, let him pull away now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: telling him the מצוות gives him a fair chance to back out before it is too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once someone converts, he is a full Jew and cannot undo it. So it is better that a person who is not serious leaves now, rather than converting and then failing to keep the מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulls away, withdraws
Let him withdraw

phrases.english: So that if he withdraws, let him withdraw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The purpose is to let an uncommitted candidate drop out before conversion.

steps.title: רבי חלבו: converts are hard on ישראל like a ספחת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the answer with רבי חלבו's teaching that converts are as hard for ישראל as a skin sore, learned from a wordplay in a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חלבו said: Converts are as hard for ישראל as a ספחת (a skin sore), as it says: 'And the גר will join them, and they will attach (ונספחו) to the house of יעקב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the idea that we should let a weak candidate leave, by quoting רבי חלבו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ונספחו ("attach") sounds like ספחת, a skin sore. Since bringing in a convert who is not truly committed can cause harm, the בית דין is careful to let such a person back out.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of skin sore (a kind of צרעת)
"And they will attach": sounds like ספחת
Hard, harmful

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥelbo said:
Converts are as hard for Israel as a skin sore,
as it is written: "And the convert will join them
and they will attach to the house of Jacob."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 14:1. The proof is the sound: ונספחו sounds like ספחת, the skin sore.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 10 with an earlier teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That it is better for an uncommitted candidate to withdraw.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חלבו's teaching, based on the wordplay ונספחו / ספחת in ישעיהו 14:1.

steps.title: He is warned about the gifts to the poor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the בית דין tells him about the sin of not giving לקט, שכחה, פאה and מעשר עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they let him know about the sin connected with לקט, שכחה, פאה and מעשר עני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. This sets up the question of why these particular מצוות are singled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of all the מצוות, the ברייתא names the gifts a farmer must leave or give to the poor. That choice needs an explanation, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin (of not keeping these מצוות)
Stalks that fall during harvest, left for the poor
Sheaves forgotten in the field, left for the poor
The corner of the field, left for the poor
The tithe given to the poor

phrases.english: And they inform him of the sin of gleanings, forgotten sheaves,
and the corner of the field, and the poor man's tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדִיעִים אוֹתוֹ עֲוֹן לֶקֶט שִׁכְחָה וּפֵאָה וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גר is specifically told about the gifts to the poor.

steps.title: Why these מצוות in particular?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא singles out the gifts to the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why these specific מצוות are mentioned. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are many serious מצוות, so naming these particular ones needs a reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the gifts to the poor are specifically mentioned to the גר.

steps.title: A בן נח is strict about even tiny amounts of property
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that a בן נח is put to death for stealing even less than a פרוטה, and returning it does not help. So a non-Jew is used to treating every bit of property with great strictness, and he must know that as a Jew he will have to give some away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A בן נח is put to death for stealing even less than a פרוטה's worth, and it is not something that can be fixed by returning it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the poor-gifts are mentioned, by quoting רבי יוחנן's rule about a בן נח and stealing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a non-Jew, even a tiny amount of property is treated with great strictness. Now that he is joining the Jewish people, he must be told that he will have to leave parts of his crop for others, which may be hard for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew, bound by the seven מצוות of בני נח
Is put to death
Less than the value of a פרוטה, the smallest coin
To be returned

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן נֹחַ נֶהֱרָג עַל פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה —
phrases.english: A non-Jew is put to death for stealing less than a peruta's worth,
and it is not subject to being returned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because a non-Jew is held to great strictness over even tiny amounts of property, the גר must be told that Jewish law requires him to give part of his crop to the poor.

steps.title: Don't overload him or be too exacting
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the בית דין does not pile too much on him and is not overly exacting with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: (And they let him know about the sin of שכחה and פאה.) And they do not pile too much on him, and they are not too exacting with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, which sets a limit: the warnings should not become a way of pushing him away. This sets up רבי אלעזר's source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the warnings, the ברייתא balances things out. The בית דין tells him enough to be honest, but does not flood him with threats or fine details that would scare off a sincere person.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not pile too much on him
They are not overly exacting with him

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the earlier warnings. He is still told the מצוות; the point is only not to overdo it and scare away a sincere גר.

phrases.english: (And they inform him of the sin of forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field.)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; they just repeat the line from before.

phrases.english: And they do not pile too much on him,
and they are not exacting with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַרְבִּים עָלָיו וְאֵין מְדַקְדְּקִים עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, adding a limit to the warnings of steps 8 and 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית דין must not overwhelm the גר or be overly exacting with him.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source: נעמי stopped arguing with רות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings the פסוק where נעמי saw that רות was determined to go with her, and stopped talking her out of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: What is the source? As it says: 'And she saw that she was determined to go with her, and she stopped speaking to her.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the פסוק that teaches the rule of not overloading a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נעמי tried to talk רות out of coming along, but once she saw רות was firm, she stopped. In the same way, a בית דין warns the candidate, but once he shows he is serious, they stop pushing him away.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is the פסוק?": the source in the תנ"ך
Determined, holding firm
And she stopped

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: What is the verse?
As it is written: "And she saw that she was determined
to go with her, and she stopped speaking to her."
phrases.notes: רות 1:18. נעמי is the one who saw, and רות is the one who was determined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we do not overload or over-pressure a sincere גר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רות 1:18: נעמי stopped trying to talk רות out of it once she saw her determination.

steps.title: Rebuilding the talk between נעמי and רות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads רות's famous words as answers to נעמי's warnings: נעמי mentions תחום שבת, and רות says 'Where you go I will go'; נעמי mentions יחוד, and רות says 'Where you lodge I will lodge.'
steps.simpleTranslation: נעמי said to her: We are not allowed to go past the תחום שבת. רות answered: 'Where you go, I will go.' נעמי said: We are not allowed to be alone (יחוד) with a man. רות answered: 'Where you lodge, I will lodge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the conversation behind the פסוקים, showing how נעמי told רות some מצוות and how רות accepted each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line רות says in the פסוק is read as a reply to a specific מצוה נעמי told her. This is the model for the בית דין: tell the candidate some מצוות, and see whether the person accepts them.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is forbidden for us"
The limit of how far one may walk on שבת
Being alone with a person of the other gender whom one may not be with
You will lodge, spend the night

steps.whatToRemember: The בית דין warns a would-be גר honestly (some light and some serious מצוות, and the gifts to the poor) so that someone who isn't serious can back out. But they don't overdo it: like נעמי with רות, once the person shows real determination, they stop pushing him away.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לַהּ: אֲסִיר לַן תְּחוּם שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: She said to her: The Shabbat limit is forbidden to us.
phrases.notes: נעמי is speaking to רות. She means we may not walk past the שבת limit.

phrases.english: "Where you go, I will go."
phrases.notes: רות 1:16. These are רות's answers, taken straight from the פסוק.

phrases.english: Being alone with a man is forbidden to us.
"Where you lodge, I will lodge."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לַהּ אֲסִיר לַן תְּחוּם שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the story behind רבי אלעזר's פסוק, showing what נעמי said before she stopped.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רות's words in the פסוק are read as acceptance of the מצוות נעמי told her, like a גר accepting מצוות before the בית דין.

steps.title: נעמי's last warnings and רות's answers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues pairing נעמי's warnings with רות's answers: 613 מצוות, עבודה זרה, four death penalties, and two burial places.
steps.simpleTranslation: נעמי said: We are commanded in 613 מצוות. רות answered: 'Your people are my people.' נעמי said: Idol worship is forbidden to us. רות answered: 'Your God is my God.' נעמי said: Four kinds of death penalty were given to the בית דין. רות answered: 'Where you die, I will die.' נעמי said: Two burial places were given to the בית דין. רות answered: 'And there I will be buried.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading רות's famous words as answers to נעמי. Each time נעמי names a hard part of being Jewish, רות answers with a phrase from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the list from step 17. נעמי is doing what the ברייתא says a בית דין should do: tell the convert some of the hard מצוות and the punishments. Each of רות's phrases shows she accepts that specific item.

keyTerms.meaning: We are commanded
It is forbidden to us
The four kinds of death penalty a בית דין can carry out
Were handed over to the court
Two burial places for people the court put to death

phrases.aramaic: מִפַּקְדִינַן שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מִצְוֹת —
phrases.english: [נעמי said:] We are commanded in six hundred and thirteen מצוות.
[רות answered:] "Your people are my people."
phrases.notes: רות 1:16

phrases.english: [נעמי said:] Idol worship is forbidden to us.
[רות answered:] "And your God is my God."
[נעמי said:] Four kinds of death penalty were handed over to the court.
[רות answered:] "Where you die, I will die."
phrases.notes: רות 1:17

phrases.english: [נעמי said:] Two burial places were handed over to the court.
phrases.notes: One place was for people put to death for more serious sins, and one was for less serious ones.

phrases.english: [רות answered:] "And there I will be buried."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפַּקְדִינַן שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of warning-and-answer pairs that began in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רות's words in the פסוק answer, one by one, נעמי's warnings about 613 מצוות, עבודה זרה, the death penalties and the burial places.

steps.title: נעמי stops trying to turn her away
steps.stepSummary: Right after רות's answers, the פסוק says נעמי saw she was determined, so נעמי stopped talking to her about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away: "And she saw that she was determined" (and she stopped speaking to her).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story. Once רות accepted everything, נעמי saw she was serious and stopped warning her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to רבי אלעזר's פסוק in step 16. The word 'immediately' shows that the list of warnings was what made נעמי see רות's determination. It also supports the ברייתא's rule that we tell a convert some מצוות but do not pile on too much.

keyTerms.meaning: Immediately, right away
Determined, firmly set on something

steps.whatToRemember: נעמי's talk with רות is the model for how a בית דין speaks to a convert: tell him the main hard points, and once he shows he is determined, stop.

phrases.english: Immediately,
"And she saw that she was determined, etc."
phrases.notes: רות 1:18. The "etc." stands for the end of the פסוק: "and she stopped speaking to her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the dialogue from steps 17-18 by returning to the פסוק רבי אלעזר quoted in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After רות accepted all the warnings, נעמי saw she was determined and stopped trying to turn her away.

steps.title: If he accepts, he is circumcised right away
steps.stepSummary: Back to the ברייתא: if the convert accepts everything, they do his מילה immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he accepts, they circumcise him right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא about the convert and quotes its next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the ברייתא described what the בית דין tells the convert. Now it moves to action: once he accepts, the מילה is done right away, with no waiting period.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted (the מצוות and what comes with them)
They circumcise him

phrases.english: If he accepted, they circumcise him immediately.
phrases.notes: We are back in the ברייתא about the convert from the earlier steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רות story and goes back to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the convert accepts, his מילה is done immediately.

steps.title: Why the rush?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the מילה must be done right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says 'immediately.' This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think it is better to wait and make sure the convert is serious. The גמרא wants to know the source of the urgency.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the convert's מילה must be done immediately rather than later.

steps.title: We do not delay a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we do not hold off doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not delay a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a מצוה that can be done now should not be pushed off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The convert's מילה is a מצוה, and once he has accepted, nothing is holding it back. So the general rule of not delaying מצוות applies, and it is done right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Delaying a מצוה
We do not delay

steps.whyThisMatters: 'We do not delay a מצוה' is a general principle that comes up in many places, not just here.

phrases.english: We do not delay a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מילה is done right away because a מצוה should not be delayed.

steps.title: Leftover shreds that block the מילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: if shreds of skin remain that make the מילה not count, he is circumcised again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If shreds remained on him that invalidate the מילה, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the ברייתא. It is setting up the next step, where it explains which shreds it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that a מילה with certain leftover skin does not count, so he needs a second cut. The ברייתא does not say which shreds count, so the גמרא will define them next.

keyTerms.meaning: Shreds or small strips of the foreskin left after the מילה
That hold back or invalidate (the מילה)

phrases.english: If there remained on him shreds
that invalidate the מילה, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of the line: he is circumcised a second time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the ברייתא after the 'circumcise him immediately' discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If shreds that invalidate the מילה remain, the convert is circumcised again.

steps.title: A משנה defines the shreds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the term using a משנה: the shreds that matter are skin covering most of the עטרה, and while they remain he may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: These are the shreds that invalidate the מילה: flesh that covers most of the עטרה. And he may not eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to explain which 'shreds' the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every bit of leftover skin is a problem. Only skin that covers most of the עטרה makes the מילה not count. Such a person still counts as an ערל, so if he is a כהן he cannot eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The crown, the rim at the head of the organ
That covers
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which only a כהן may eat

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in שבת 137a.

phrases.english: These are the shreds that invalidate the מילה:
flesh that covers most of the עטרה.
And he may not eat תרומה.
phrases.notes: With these shreds he still counts as uncircumcised, so a כהן in this state cannot eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן אֵלּוּ הֵן צִיצִין הַמְעַכְּבִין הַמִּילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the term 'shreds that invalidate' from the ברייתא in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shreds that invalidate the מילה are flesh covering most of the עטרה; while they remain he may not eat תרומה.

steps.title: רב adds: covering most of the height
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא quotes רב: flesh covering most of the height of the עטרה also invalidates the מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: flesh that covers most of the height of the עטרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's explanation of the משנה, which adds another case of shreds that block the מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'most of the עטרה,' which could mean most of the way around it. רב adds that skin covering most of the עטרה's height also counts, even if it does not go most of the way around. That widens the set of shreds that require cutting again.

keyTerms.meaning: Its height
An אמורא who passes on teachings of רב

steps.whatToRemember: A convert is circumcised right away because we do not delay a מצוה. If shreds remain that cover most of the עטרה, whether most of the way around or most of its height, the מילה does not count and he must be circumcised again.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And רב ירמיה בר אבא said that רב said:

phrases.aramaic: בָּשָׂר הַחוֹפֶה רוֹב גּוֹבְהָהּ שֶׁל עֲטָרָה.
phrases.english: Flesh that covers most of the height of the עטרה.
phrases.notes: He means this case also blocks the מילה, even if the skin does not go most of the way around.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רב's explanation to the משנה quoted in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flesh covering most of the height of the עטרה also counts as shreds that invalidate the מילה.

steps.title: Once healed, he is immersed right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: after the מילה heals, the גר is immersed immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he has healed, they immerse him right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the ברייתא: after the convert's מילה heals, he goes to the מקוה right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the order: first מילה, then healing, then טבילה. The word 'immediately' fits the earlier idea that we do not hold off doing a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: he has healed
they immerse (in a מקוה)
immediately

phrases.english: Once he has healed, they immerse him immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא after the discussion of shreds of skin from the מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the מילה heals, the convert is immersed without delay.

steps.title: Only after healing: why?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads closely: only when he has healed is he immersed, not before. It asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he healed, yes. If he did not heal, no. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices the ברייתא says 'once healed.' That means we do not immerse him before he heals, and the גמרא asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question comes from the exact wording. If healing were not needed, the ברייתא could have said to immerse him right after the מילה. So healing must matter, and the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: yes
what is the reason?

phrases.english: If he has healed, yes,
if he has not healed, no.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְרַפֵּא אִין לֹא נִתְרַפֵּא לָא מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a close reading from the line just quoted and asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why must the convert wait until he heals before immersing?

steps.title: Water irritates a wound
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that water irritates a fresh wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because water irritates a wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we wait because water makes a fresh wound hurt and get worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wait is not a rule about the conversion itself. It is about the convert's health and comfort. Once he heals, the water does no harm, so he immerses right away.

keyTerms.meaning: water
irritate, aggravate
a wound

phrases.english: Because water irritates a wound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We wait for healing because water aggravates an open wound.

steps.title: Two scholars stand over him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: two תלמידי חכמים stand over the convert as he immerses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And two Torah scholars stand over him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: two תלמידי חכמים stand by during the טבילה. This line will be challenged next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars are there to oversee the טבילה. The number 'two' is what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah scholars
over him, beside him

phrases.english: And two Torah scholars
stand over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים עוֹמְדִים עַל גַּבָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars must be present at the convert's טבילה.

steps.title: But a convert needs three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges 'two': רבי יוחנן said a גר needs three, a full בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חייא say in the name of רבי יוחנן that a convert needs three?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the number in the ברייתא. רבי יוחנן ruled that conversion needs three people, not two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Conversion is done by a בית דין, and a בית דין has three judges. So a ברייתא that says two seems to go against רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't (he) say? (opens a challenge)
a convert
three (a בית דין)

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya say
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A convert requires three!
phrases.notes: Three people make a בית דין, a court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number given in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that two scholars are enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן requires three for conversion, so 'two' clashes with an established rule.

steps.title: Fix the text: read three
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן himself told the reciter to change the ברייתא to say three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן told the reciter: teach 'three.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wording of the ברייתא is corrected. רבי יוחנן told the תנא who recited it to say 'three' instead of 'two.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real argument here, because the wording of the ברייתא is fixed. With the correction, the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן agree that three are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: a reciter who memorized and taught ברייתות
teach / recite (it this way)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this answer argues that two is enough. The answer changes the text of the ברייתא to 'three.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to the reciter:
Teach: three.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְתַנָּא תְּנִי שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says only two scholars are needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should read 'three,' which matches רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: After immersing, he is fully Jewish
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: once he has immersed and come up, he is like a Jew in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he immersed and came up, he is like a Jew in all matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line: as soon as the convert comes out of the מקוה, he is completely Jewish. The גמרא will next ask what this adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טבילה is the final step that finishes the conversion. The phrase 'in every sense' is broad, and the גמרא will want to know which practical law it is pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: immersed and came up
like a Jew
in all his matters

phrases.english: Once he immersed and came up
he is like a Jew in all his matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָבַל וְעָלָה הֲרֵי הוּא כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְכׇל דְּבָרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next line of the ברייתא, after the scholars at the טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After טבילה, the convert is a full Jew.

steps.title: What practical law does this teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what law is meant by 'like a Jew in every sense.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law is this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference the phrase 'like a Jew in every sense' makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is obvious that a convert is Jewish. So the גמרא looks for the specific case where saying so teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: for what law? (what is the practical point?)

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical point of step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law follows from calling the convert 'like a Jew in every sense'?

steps.title: Even if he goes back, his קידושין work
steps.stepSummary: If he returns to his old ways and betroths a Jewish woman, he counts as a Jew who left the path (ישראל משומד), and his קידושין are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he turns back and betroths a Jewish woman, we call him a Jewish מומר, and his betrothal is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase teaches that the conversion can never be undone. Even if he later abandons Judaism, he is still a Jew, so his קידושין take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who is not Jewish cannot make קידושין with a Jewish woman. Because this convert's קידושין do take effect, we see that he is still Jewish, just a sinning one, a ישראל משומד. Going back to his old ways does not cancel the conversion.

keyTerms.meaning: he turned back, went back to his old ways
betroths
a Jew who has left Torah observance
betrothal

steps.whatToRemember: Once a גר has immersed, his conversion stands for good. Even if he goes back to his old ways, he is a Jew in the eyes of הלכה, and his קידושין are valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that conversion is a permanent change of status, not something that depends on how he behaves later.

phrases.english: That if he turns back
and betroths a Jewish woman,
we call him a Jew who has abandoned the faith,
and his betrothal is a valid betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי הָדַר בֵּיהּ וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If he goes back to his old ways, he remains a Jew, and his קידושין to a Jewish woman are valid.

steps.title: Same for a convert and a freed slave
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: this applies to both a גר and an עבד משוחרר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both a convert and a freed slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line, which puts a convert and a freed slave together. The גמרא is setting up a question about what exactly they share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Canaanite slave who is freed becomes a full Jew, like a convert. The ברייתא does not say in which way the two are alike, and that gap leads to the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a freed (Canaanite) slave
both... and...

phrases.english: Both a convert and a freed slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The conversion laws of the ברייתא apply in some way to a freed slave as well.

steps.title: Does a freed slave accept the מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא means both must accept the מצוות‎ (קבלת עול מצות), that clashes with another ברייתא saying a freed slave does not need to.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think it means accepting the yoke of מצוות. But another ברייתא says: this is said about a convert, but a freed slave does not need to accept.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא means both the convert and the freed slave must accept the מצוות. Then it challenges this with another ברייתא that says a freed slave does not need to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other ברייתא limits the need to accept מצוות to a convert and says a freed slave does not need it. If our ברייתא puts the freed slave together with the convert for accepting מצוות, it clashes with that ברייתא. The next step answers the clash.

keyTerms.meaning: it could enter your mind (a first guess)
the yoke of מצוות
and they pointed out a contradiction
in what case are these words said?

phrases.english: It could enter your mind
that it means for accepting upon himself the yoke of מצוות.
phrases.notes: He means the two are alike in that both must accept the מצוות at the time of טבילה.

phrases.english: But a contradiction was raised:
In what case are these words said? With a convert,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּעֶבֶד מְשׁוּחְרָר — אֵין צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל!
phrases.english: but a freed slave does not need to accept!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל מִצְוֹת וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a reading of step 35 and challenges it with another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that a convert and a freed slave are alike in accepting the מצוות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says only a convert must accept the מצוות and a freed slave need not, so the two cannot be alike in this way.

steps.title: רב ששת: the two ברייתות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers the contradiction from the previous step. The ברייתא saying a freed slave does not need קבלת עול מצות follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The ברייתא implying he does need it follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is not a problem. This ברייתא follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and that ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת settles the clash between the two ברייתות. He says they do not really contradict each other, because each one follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not force both ברייתות into one opinion. Instead, it sends them to two sides of a known מחלוקת. The one that frees a slave without קבלת מצות matches רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The one that requires it matches the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem. This phrase opens an answer that removes a contradiction.
A תנא whose view will turn out to be lenient here.
The Rabbis, meaning the majority or unnamed opinion in a ברייתא.
This one ... that one. Used to assign each source to a different case or opinion.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: It is not difficult:
This one is Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא saying a freed slave doesn't need to accept the מצוות.

phrases.english: that one is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each ברייתא to a different תנא (תנאי היא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות must follow one opinion, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow two different תנאים, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: The רבנן's view on the יפת תואר
steps.stepSummary: The source for the מחלוקת is a ברייתא about the יפת תואר. The process of crying for her parents applies when she did not accept the מצוות. If she did accept them, he immerses her and may marry her right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And she shall bewail her father and her mother, etc.' When is this said? When she did not accept the מצוות. But if she accepted them, he immerses her and is permitted to her immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings the ברייתא that shows the two opinions he just mentioned. This first part gives the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the quick way to marry her depends on her accepting the מצוות. Only then does the טבילה make her permitted immediately. This shows that for the רבנן, acceptance of מצוות matters for this kind of טבילה. That is the view behind the ברייתא that requires קבלת מצות.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא. This introduces a source.
The beautiful captive woman taken in war, whom the Torah allows a soldier to marry after a set process.
In what case are these words said? This limits the rule just stated.
She accepted upon herself the מצוות.
He immerses her in a מקוה.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"And she shall bewail her father and her mother, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 21:13. This is about the captive woman, the יפת תואר.

phrases.english: Under what circumstance are these matters stated?
When she did not accept upon herself.
phrases.notes: The word left out is the מצוות: she did not accept the מצוות.

phrases.english: But if she accepted upon herself,
he immerses her, and he is permitted to her immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source showing the מחלוקת that רב ששת relied on.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן require acceptance of מצוות for the טבילה to work fully.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: immersion for slavery, then for freedom
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that even if she did not accept the מצוות, he can force her to immerse as a שפחה. Then he immerses her again for freedom and frees her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Even if she did not accept the מצוות, he forces her and immerses her for slavery, then immerses her again for freedom, and frees her.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second opinion in the ברייתא, the view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. His sentence continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a טבילה for freedom works even with no acceptance of מצוות. So a freed slave does not need קבלת עול מצות. This is exactly the view behind the ברייתא that said he does not need it.

keyTerms.meaning: He forces her.
For the sake of slavery, making her a שפחה.
For the sake of being freed.
He frees her.

steps.confusionAlert: A forced first טבילה does not make her a convert. It only makes her a שפחה. It is the second טבילה, together with freeing her, that makes her Jewish.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the clear source that a freed slave can become Jewish without accepting the מצוות. It explains the ברייתא that said he does not need קבלת עול מצות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא קִבְּלָה עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: Even if she did not accept upon herself,
he forces her and immerses her for the sake of slavery,
and then he again immerses her for the sake of emancipation,
and emancipates her,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion in the same ברייתא, completing רב ששת's proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a טבילה for freedom works without קבלת מצות, according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same ברייתא about יפת תואר.
